card: This PR enables the optin.performance.Padding clang-tidy check at a 24-byte threshold and reorders member variables in CBlockIndex, CNode, CConnman, CTxMemPool, CWalletTx, Peer, and CRPCConvertParam to eliminate existing padding warnings. It aims to reduce memory usage in long-lived structures and automatically prevent future struct layout regressions. The author notes that reducing CBlockIndex padding alone saves roughly 8MB of RAM at block height 1M. It is based on and includes work from PR 36501.
evidence: Commit c2dedba48f notes that for CBlockIndex, 'Moving one field somewhere else makes the class lose less bytes due to padding... For a ~1M block height, this saves about 8M of Ram without doing anything else.'
PR description explains the motivation: 'Enabling it at this point would be to catch regressions above this amount.'
problem: Inefficient struct layout introduces excess memory padding across frequently allocated or long-lived data structures, wasting memory. Without automated tooling, new or modified structures can introduce large padding inefficiencies unnoticed.

risk.why: Member reordering without logic changes is unlikely to cause bugs unless struct memory layout is relied on by serialization or atomic operations.

scope_notes: This RFC includes reordering member fields across validation, networking, mempool, wallet, and RPC data structures before enabling the clang-tidy analyzer check.
summary: This pull request enables the `optin.performance.Padding` clang-tidy check with an explicit threshold of 24 bytes to catch struct padding regressions. It reorders member fields across several internal data structures—including CBlockIndex, CNode, CConnman, CTxMemPool, CWalletTx, Peer, and CRPCConvertParam—to eliminate padding warnings that exceed the threshold.
uncertainties: The patch was omitted from the prompt, so the exact field reorderings cannot be directly inspected.
